subject: POC prompt & eval dataset collection - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmehealth.com>, Emily Ortiz <emily.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: POC prompt & eval dataset collection - next steps

Hi Sam / Emily,

Thanks again for the time today - great conversation and very aligned on success criteria for the POC. Quick recap and next steps so we have a single source of truth:

- POC goal: Reduce triage time for support articles by surfacing top-1 suggested KB article for user questions and improve precision/recall vs current rule-based matcher.
- Success criteria (proposal): p95 latency < 300ms, relative improvement in top-1 accuracy >= 20% on your held-out prompt set, and human-rated relevance >= 4/5 on a 200-sample eval set.
- Timeline: target sandbox start week of May 18-20, 3-4 week eval window, checkpoint after 2 weeks for early signals.
- Ownership: Sam (ML Lead) will own prompt/log delivery; Emily (Head of Data) will own business validation & human rater coordination. Redwood: Marissa (sales) + Rishi (SE) + Dev (solutions) for setup and eval harness.

What we need from your side to start the POC work:
1) Prompt & log set: sample prompts and anonymized user logs (CSV preferred). We included a short template in the attached "poc-eval-plan-template.pdf" that defines columns we expect (prompt_id, prompt_text, context, expected_label, confidence, timestamp).
2) Success criteria confirmation: confirm the metrics above or share alternate KPIs you want us to measure.
3) Timeline confirmation: can you confirm a preferred start date between May 18-20 and a target end date?
4) Ownership & access: who will upload data, and what access method do you prefer (S3 presigned, secure SFTP, or Drive)? We can provide a secure presigned S3 endpoint and non-production retention policy details.

Attaching the POC eval plan template to make this easier. If you can upload an initial prompt/label sample (50-200 rows) by May 15 that will let Rishi spin up the evaluation harness and give early signals before the full sandbox start.

Proposed next meeting: Kickoff + runbook review on Tue May 19, 10:00am PT (30 min). If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks - looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: poc-eval-plan-template.pdf (template, 2 pages)

Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700

Thanks Marissa - appreciate the clear recap.

Quick answers:
- We can own prompt/log delivery. I (Sam) will be the primary contact for the ML artifacts; Emily will own business validation.
- Timeline: May 20 start looks good for us; target end date June 17 (4 weeks) to allow time for business validation.
- Data: We will provide anonymized user logs + labeled examples. For initial upload I attached a small CSV with 100 anonymized prompts (acme_prompts_v1.csv). It follows most of the template columns, and includes a small sample of multi-turn contexts.
- Questions: 1) Do you need PII redaction guidance from our side or will Redwood do additional sanitization? 2) Can the evaluation harness handle multi-turn prompts/conversation history?

We value the 20% improvement target but we'll confirm after the first 200-sample sanity check.

Sam Jenkins

sam.jenkins@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Emily Ortiz <emily.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC prompt & eval dataset collection - next steps

Thanks Sam - got the CSV and appreciate the fast turnaround. A few clarifications and the plan from our side:

- PII/Redaction: Please remove direct identifiers before upload (emails, SSNs, PHI). Redwood will run an automated scrub for anything we detect in the sandbox but we prefer customer-side redaction for production data. If you want, our security team can share a short checklist.

- Multi-turn support: Yes - our evaluation harness supports multi-turn contexts. In the template, include a "context" column with previous turns concatenated (we provided a max token guidance). For model scoring, we'll evaluate on the full context + prompt as a single test case.

- Evaluation metrics (we suggest measuring):
  * Latency: p50/p95 token latency and end-to-end response time (target p95 < 300ms).
  * Relevance/Accuracy: top-1 exact match and top-3 recall on labeled examples.
  * Business score: 200 human-rated samples (1-5) with 4/5 as pass threshold.
  * Degression checks: run pre-POC baseline against your current system and report relative lift.

- Next steps & owners:
  * Acme: upload initial CSV (50-200 rows) by 2026-05-15. Sam to confirm upload method.
  * Redwood: Rishi to instrument evaluation harness and provide a short runbook + mapping (expected 3 business days after we receive sample).
  * Scheduling: Kickoff May 19, 10:00am PT.

Rishi / Dev - can you prepare the eval harness and a mapping doc (columns -> eval fields)? Rishi, if you can include an initial baseline run against their sample once uploaded that would be great.

Thanks - I'll follow up with a calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa

- We will provide an initial 200-row labeled set and an anonymized 2k-row log sample by Friday May 15.
- A couple clarifying Qs:
  1) For multi-turn contexts, do you prefer a single concatenated string or a JSON blob per row? CSV is easiest for our team but can adapt.
  2) Will Redwood produce per-prompt scoring (CSV with prompt_id -> score) as output so our analysts can join back to labels?

Security: our security team will want an upload mechanism that supports pre-signed S3 + AES-256 at rest. Can you share S3 presigned instructions or an SFTP endpoint? We can also route via our secure file exchange.

Appreciate the clear criteria. We'll make sure the human rater guidelines are aligned with the business score metric.

Thanks team - short update and concrete next actions.

1) Upload method: We can accept a pre-signed S3 upload. I've asked our security ops (security-ops@redwood.com) to generate a short-lived presigned bucket for your sandbox uploads and will share the link via secure email within 24 hours. Files should be AES-256 encrypted at rest; we will add a retention note in the bucket (sandbox data will be auto-deleted after 30 days).

2) Format: Please upload CSV with the following columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, context, expected_label, label_confidence, timestamp. For multi-turn please concatenate turns with "\n" between turns (CSV-friendly). If you prefer JSON per-row we can accept that as a .jsonl file - notify us in advance.

3) Security checklist: Customer-side redaction preferred. Our security ops will still run automated scrub and provide a short findings report. If your security team wants the checklist, loop them to security-ops@redwood.com.

4) Deliverables & deadlines:
   * Acme: Upload initial sample (50-200 rows) to presigned S3 by 2026-05-15.
   * Redwood: Rishi to run a baseline evaluation within 3 business days of upload and share initial metrics + mapping doc.
   * Kickoff: May 19, 10:00am PT (calendar invite to follow).

Internal note for Rishi/Dev: Please prepare the evaluation harness with multi-turn support and provide a mapping template (columns -> eval fields) and a sample output CSV (prompt_id, predicted_label, score, latency_ms). Rishi - I'll leave the technical details to you to confirm.

If all good, I'll send the calendar invite and a short Doc with the evaluation plan (link will be attached to the invite).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
